items.title: The first 30 seconds show the title's promise, said and on screen
items.detail: YouTube's Intro key moment is the share of viewers still watching after 30 s, and YouTube's own help page says a high Intro means 'the content in the first 30 seconds matched the viewer's expectation of the video's thumbnail and title' (support.google.com/youtube/answer/9314415). Studio: the title's claim (e.g. 'lost to its own loan', 'paid to destroy its own toys', 'the filing blamed your face') is spoken in its own meaning and its object or document is on screen by 10 s, and the thumbnail's object is frame 1 or appears by 10 s. Each outlined topic in longform/topics.json already has this in its cold-open line. Know it worked: Intro (retention at 30 s) on our long videos, compared across them.

items.title: Test: the whole rise and fall inside the first 30 s instead of by 50 s
items.detail: The recipe's arc tells the rise and fall by 50 s and the one-cause promise by ~65 s; YouTube measures the intro at 30 s. The reference with the earliest turn, Bagholder's KFC (591K on 10.8K), reaches 'but at home…' at 19 s and the ranking chart by 26-36 s (style-study 2026-11-19 section 4). Challenger: the fall's figure lands by 25-30 s, the promise stays at ~60 s. Judge on Intro (retention at 30 s) and on held-after-the-hook, per side, in the long videos' own test; needs 4+ long videos a side.

items.title: Record Intro (retention at 30 s) for every long video
items.detail: metrics/videos.json has hookHold, endHold and stayed, but no long video's share still watching at 30 s, which is YouTube's Intro measure and the one a long hook test needs. Add `intro` to each long video's row from the retention curve the stats job already pulls (the point nearest 30 s). Craze & Crash has no long video out yet, so it can be added before the first one. Know it worked: the field appears on the first long video's row 48 h after it goes out.

items.title: First recap-and-tease before the payoff, then one every 2-3 minutes
items.detail: Both films so far had their first recap at 57-59% (Crocs 8:40 of 15:07, Pizza Hut vs Domino's 9:59 of 16:47), so viewers went 7.5-8.5 minutes with no 'so far' and no stated reason to stay. The scout spec and recipe ask for a recap-and-tease every 2-3 minutes. Studio: put a one-sentence 'so far … but' line at about 25-35% (just before the payoff chapter), and one more every 2-3 minutes after; keep each to one or two sentences (a long recap is itself a skip point). Check: in the script, no 3-minute stretch between chapter 1 and the ending without a recap or tease line; later, audience retention between 30% and 60% once the films have views.

items.title: Answer the question in under 40 s, without a separate 'what happened' chapter
items.detail: The endings run 77 s (Crocs, from 13:50) and 100 s (Pizza Hut, its own 'Chapter eight' card at 90%). Audiences leave as soon as a story resolves, and a chapter card that promises a lesson reads as the end. Test: no chapter card for the ending; the mechanism in one or two lines straight after the last fact, then the comment question and end screen, all in 40 s or less. Judge on end hold / average view percentage of the long videos with and without it (long videos' own test).

items.title: Record where long viewers leave, chapter by chapter
items.detail: YouTube's key moments report marks dips (viewers leaving or skipping) and spikes (rewatching, which can also mean confusion). For each long video, store the retention curve's biggest dips and spikes with the beat on screen (like analysis/pictures.json for Shorts), so the next scout Tuesday-focus run can say which chapter starts lose people. Where: the stats worker and metrics/videos.json for format long (auditor lane). Done when L-20261123-31 has a dips list once it has enough views.

items.title: Doc beats: an event can only name a word's first occurrence
items.detail: In L-20261127-31 two cuts landed on the wrong word because the word appeared earlier in the line ('So why toys? ... came back for toys' cut on the first 'toys'; 'So was it Amazon ... and Amazon' put the Amazon label on the Walmart photo). QA caught both on the stills. Fix (improver): let an event name its occurrence ({"word": "toys", "nth": 2}) in renderer/timeline/build.py, and have lint warn when an event's word occurs more than once in the line.

items.title: Doc overlays: a minimum time on screen, and leave before the next overlay
items.detail: QA on L-20261127-31 took four rounds mostly on overlay timing: labels left on after a cut, then (once given outs) labels on screen under 0.8 s, and stamps landing on the figure they were meant to sell. Fix (improver): in DocBeat/lint, hold every label, stamp and date at least 1.5 s, end it before the next overlay in the same corner lands, and never let a stamp cover a count-up or a highlighted document line.

items.title: The split layer draws its names and figures inside the long video's caption band
items.detail: In L-20261127-31 (payoff, what-if) the captions landed between the split's two figures. Studio replaced both splits with count-ups and a chart. Fix (improver): the split's names and figures sit above the caption zone in a 1920x1080 doc beat.
